top.title: Michael Carrick has painfully awkward exchange with interviewer over Man United future
top.description: Michael Carrick endured an awkward end to a post-match interview as he had an excruciating exchange about his future as Manchester United manager. Carrick had just watched his United side fight back from 4-2 down in injury time to snatch the unlikeliest of 4-4 draws with Aston Villa , having earlier come back from being 2-0 behind inside five minutes. It was a real mixed display from the Red Devils, who showed plenty of heart and character but had put themselves in bad positions due to consistently disastrous defending. The result – combined with their incredible comeback victory against Roma in midweek – has probably saved Carrick’s job, although his United side still head into this international break in the Premier League ’s bottom three, lying 18th in the table. His long-term future appears to very much still be up in the air and his post-match interview on Sky Sports with reporter Patrick Davison was an awkward watch. Carrick firstly bristled slightly when asked if United are looking at a relegation fight, saying: “No, we’re in November. I don’t like this situation we’re in, I don’t like the results we’ve had but we can definitely do something about it.” "That's not going to happen" 🗣️ Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 8, 2026 From there, things got worse, as Davison asked a lengthy question suggesting there were clearly going to be conversations about his future during the international break over the next couple of weeks, to which Carrick simply responded: "Is there?" When it was suggested that one would assume so, Carrick tersely said: “Would you?” and when he was pushed for what he thought about his situation, the Man United boss said to Davison: “You’re telling me, what do you think”. After that, the interviewer specified that he wanted to know what Carrick expected to happen in the next couple of weeks and he then gave a longer answer admitting that it wasn’t a good situation, the team haven’t won enough games but that he expects to move forward and keep working on the things they’ve been working on until this point. Michael Carrick (Reuters) Back in the Sky Sports studio, pundit Roy Keane was asked for his thoughts on the interview as a whole and the former Man United captain compared the current boss to a politician. He said: “It’s obviously difficult for the manager, he’s under pressure no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn’t say much – maybe that’s a tactic. He’s like a politician. “He’s clearly under pressure and says he knows there are things to work on but he better get moving on that... This is their worst start in however many years.”

top.title: Caleb Williams MVP Case Hinges On Sunday Night Against Tampa Bay
top.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images A Bears victory on Sunday could push Caleb Williams into the MVP conversation. That number trails Josh Allen, Brock Purdy, and Joe Burrow, but the gap is closing fast. Since Williams came back from a hamstring injury that sidelined him during Weeks 3 through 5, the Bears have claimed three consecutive victories. Chicago has not trailed in any of those three contests and has scored more than 30 points each time. Williams has fixed the biggest issue from his rookie year. His completion percentage has jumped from 58.1 percent in 2025 to 70.9 percent this season. Yahoo Sports noted that only Joe Burrow holds a higher rate in the entire league. At Halas Hall on Wednesday, Coach Ben Johnson informed reporters that the passing operation feels much smoother. “I think our passing game in general has been a little bit cleaner,” Johnson said. Enhanced timing and confidence linking the quarterback with his leading trio of receivers fuel this progress. The Chemistry Is Real The connection between Williams and his targets has deepened beyond the field. The group spends significant time together to build that bond. Williams explained that the communication grew because they share meals and hang out. “We hang out together. We do things together. We eat together, break bread together,” Williams said. Luther Burden III showed this grit against Seattle by catching a 1-yard touchdown to end an 8-minute, 32-second opening drive. Before the catch, Burden told Williams he did not fear the defending Super Bowl champions. “I went up to him and told him I don’t care who they is,” the wide receiver said. Williams stood up from the bench and yelled back, “I don’t give a f— who they are!” Blocking Wins Games Too The offense also relies on the receivers to do the dirty work. Rome Odunze is the key player in this new dynamic. He cleared a path for a 39-yard screen pass against Seattle that sealed the win. Kalif Raymond ran through the tunnel because Odunze made the block. “If [Odunze] doesn’t get that block, the screen doesn’t go,” Raymond said. With 14 receptions totaling 234 yards in each half, Odunze is heading toward his finest campaign in three years. On Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET, they face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field. TSN noted that Tampa Bay yields just 18.9 points per game, which is the fifth-best mark in the league.

top.title: Inter player ratings vs Como: Marcus Thuram leads the charge in commanding San Siro victory
top.description: FC Internazionale v Como 1907 - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Inter Milan produced a clinical first-half display to secure a 2-0 victory over Como at the Giuseppe Meazza. Goals from Francesco Esposito and Marcus Thuram proved decisive in a match where the hosts efficiently managed their lead. Inter Milan demonstrated their tactical superiority at San Siro, securing a controlled 2-0 victory over a resilient Como side. The Nerazzurri wasted no time asserting their authority, with Francesco Esposito breaking the deadlock in the 12th minute following excellent work by Djed Spence. The pressure remained relentless, and just seven minutes later, Marcus Thuram doubled the advantage, effectively settling the contest before the twenty-minute mark. Inter's ability to compress the pitch in the middle third stifled Como's build-up play, limiting the visitors to just a single shot on target throughout the ninety minutes. Despite Como enjoying more of the ball in the second half (57% total possession), Inter remained the more dangerous side on the counter, racking up an expected goals (xG) value of 1.86 compared to the visitors' 0.20. Cristian Chivu’s side displayed impressive defensive discipline, recorded 12 interceptions and winning the majority of their physical duels. While the intensity naturally dipped after the interval, the damage done in the opening exchange ensured a comfortable evening for the reigning giants, moving them closer to the summit of the Serie A table. Goalkeeper & Defence Josep Martinez - 7/10 A largely spectator role for the Spanish goalkeeper, who was only required to make one save all afternoon. His distribution was efficient, helping Inter bypass Como's initial press, and he commanded his area well during the few crosses that bypassed the front line. Alessandro Bastoni - 7/10 Typically progressive in his passing, Bastoni acted as a secondary playmaker from the left side of the back three. He remained untroubled defensively and was key to the clean sheet, contributing to a defensive unit that allowed very little central penetration. Manuel Akanji - 7/10 The Swiss international provided the structural security Inter needed in the heart of the defence. His positioning was immaculate, ensuring that Douvikas was starved of service, and he handled the physical transitions with his usual composure. Carlos Augusto - 7/10 Slotting into the back three, Augusto showed his versatility. He was quick to cover the space behind Dimarco and was proactive in his defensive duties, helping Inter maintain their 12 interceptions as a team. Midfield Federico Dimarco - 7/10 A constant threat down the left flank until his substitution in the 87th minute. His delivery from wide areas remained a primary weapon for Inter, and his tactical discipline in tracking back prevented Yago Couto from finding any joy in the final third. Djed Spence - 8/10 An excellent performance from the wing-back, who provided the assist for the opening goal in the 12th minute

top.title: Braden Mann unleashes an 85-yard punt for Eagles
top.description: Sunday’s game against the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles has been something of a defensive struggle. So when Nick Sirianni sent Braden Mann and the rest of the Philadelphia punt team into the game with under 30 seconds left in the first half, leading 8-6 but deep in their own territory, Sirianni probably just wanted to try and get his defense into better field position. He likely did not expect Mann to pin the Giants inside New York’s own 10-yard line. But that is exactly what happened, as Mann unleashed a booming 85-yard punt that rolled out of bounds at the Giants’ 6-yard line: BRADEN MANN WHAT A PUNT NYGvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0knmQEiDKM — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The massive punt sent FOX Sports announced Joe Davis into a state of delirium, as he declared that the kick had to be “close to the longest punt in NFL history.’ Interestingly enough, however, it does not even crack the top ten! According to Pro Football Reference, the longest punt in NFL history remains this booming 98-yard punt from Steve O’Neal of the New York Jets, back in 1969. A 92-yard punt from Shawn McCarthy of the New England Patriots comes in second, while the legendary kick from Randall Cunningham of the 1989 Eagles, which covered 91 yards, comes in third. Sammy Baugh’s 1940 punt of 85 yards comes in at No. 12 on the list, which is the mark Mann tied with this kick. You can see that full list here .

top.title: Jorge Martin will be "almost 100% fit" in Portugal as heroic Qatar display keeps title hopes alive
top.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin , who finished seventh in Sunday's MotoGP race at Lusail, showcased his trademark resilience throughout the weekend in Qatar. Resilience that saw him go from considering skipping the race entirely early in the week to not only competing but delaying Marc Marquez's title celebrations. Once again, MotoGP's Asian flyaway races have proven decisive in the outcome of the world championship, which is now firmly within Marquez's grasp. The Ducati rider could be crowned champion in two weeks' time, but that he failed to seal the title in Qatar was thanks to Marco Bezzecchi's speed and Martin's resilience. Read Also: MotoGP Qatar GP: Marco Bezzecchi wins as Marc Marquez has title triumph delayed Over the course of this week, Martin went from contemplating staying in Spain and missing the race at Lusail, because of the pain caused by the fracture in his right wrist, to finishing third in Saturday's sprint and seventh in Sunday's grand prix. Despite losing further ground to Marquez, the Aprilia rider demonstrated a remarkable ability to endure pain, earning praise from most of his rivals. His achievement was all the more impressive considering he started from 11th on the grid - 10th on Sunday after Francesco Bagnaia 's withdrawal - which made his task even more difficult and increased the level of risk he had to take. "I'm proud of what I've done because on Monday and Tuesday I didn't even want to come here, and in the end I managed to finish both races," said Martin in his Spanish interview on Sunday evening. "We're going to Portugal still in with a chance. It's getting harder and harder, but we're still there." Although the injury is less serious than initially feared, the limitations it imposes on him when changing direction and braking are evident, particularly over a long run or race. Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team "I can't ride properly, I can't brake properly and I can't push the bike to the limit. It was really tough towards the end. For the last three laps, I just wanted the race to be over." In the sprint, Martin benefited from his last-minute decision to use the soft rear tyre, which allowed him to gain several positions through the opening corners. On Sunday, with everyone running the same tyre specification, the playing field was more level. "There was a lot of risk in the opening corners. The key was qualifying, because starting so far back didn't help me," explained the #89, who was physically exhausted by the end of the race. "My hand is swollen up like a melon, but I think I'll be almost 100% fit in Portugal. I'm tough and stubborn. There's something inside me that keeps pushing me to fight," concluded Martin, who will head to the Algarve circuit 60 points behind Marquez and 14 ahead of Bezzecchi. top.title: Ninkovich Unloads Brutal Truth: Kelce Is Just A Receiver
top.description: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Rob Ninkovich delivered a sharp critique of Travis Kelce during the Hall of Fame induction ceremony for Rob Gronkowski at Gillette Stadium on Saturday. The former New England Patriots linebacker stated clearly that Kelce does not measure up to Gronkowski in the eyes of those who value the blocking aspect of the position. Ninkovich attended the event where Gronkowski received his red jacket and joined the 38th member of the Patriots Hall of Fame. The comments came while Ninkovich was asked to compare the two stars who have dominated the tight end position in recent years. He did not hold back his opinion about the Kansas City Chiefs star versus the New England legend. The debate centers on what defines a complete tight end in the NFL. Ninkovich believes that receiving ability alone is not enough to claim the title of the greatest. He pointed out that Gronkowski brought a physical element to the game that Kelce has not shown in the same way. This view was shared by many fans and analysts who remember the physical play of the former Patriots star. The ceremony was a celebration of Gronkowski’s nine seasons in New England, but the comparison to his successor in popularity sparked a new discussion about the position. Ninkovich’s words were direct and focused on the specific skills required to play the role as he sees it. Ninkovich Draws a Hard Line Between the Two Stars Rob Ninkovich made his stance clear when he addressed the comparison between Travis Kelce and Rob Gronkowski during the induction speech. He told the crowd that the two players are not similar in their approach to the game. Ninkovich stated, “Kelce and [Rob Gronkowski] don’t even come close. He’s [Kelce] a receiver. This guy’s [Gronkowski] a tight end,” according to Yahoo Sports . This comment highlights the former Patriots linebacker’s belief that the definition of the position includes more than just catching passes. top.title: Match review: RSL secures 6th consecutive playoff berth in 2-1 victory over LA
top.description: Sergi Solans (22) celebrates after notching his third MLS brace and 14th goal of his rookie season. | Real Salt Lake Real Salt Lake secured a 2-1 victory and a spot in the MLS Playoffs in the high-stakes, must-win Decision Day matchup against the LA Galaxy in front of a roaring crowd of 20,738 fans at America First Field. Solans and Booth lift RSL to playoff berth Spanish sensation Sergi Solans continued his impressive rookie MLS campaign, netting his 15th goal in the 10th minute to give RSL the early lead, putting him just two goals shy of the MLS rookie regular season scoring record of 17 goals (Cyle Larin in 2015 with Orlando City SC). The scoring continued with Utah native Zach Booth netting his second goal of the 2026 season just two minutes later. With the Decision Day victory, Real Salt Lake has officially punched its ticket to the postseason for a sixth consecutive season, the longest active playoff streak in the Western Conference. Although the evening was a nail biter the home side further cemented itself as a constant within the best squads in the Western Conference, earning ninth place and a spot in the Wild Card match. Quotable “We could only do what we could, which was win the game and then the universe had to do its thing, it’s gotta cook. We were in the right spot to receive its blessings and all we talked about was controlling what we can, and tonight the guys did a great job.“ — RSL coach Pablo Mastroeni Game summary The Claret-and-Cobalt opened up the Decision Day battle with energy, pushing up the pitch immediately as Solans and Canadian defender Luc de Fougerolles each earned tangible scoring opportunities in the second and fifth minutes. Although the early momentum continued with the home side netting two goals within minutes of each other, the LA Galaxy found the back of the net in the 40th minute to make the score 2-1. After earning an impressive seven shots on target, Real Salt Lake headed into the locker room with a one goal lead. The home side continued to show grit and energy as the second half began, stringing together passes to bring the ball up the pitch and into its attacking third. In the 59th minute, RSL Head coach Pablo Mastroeni made his first substitutions of the match bringing on defensive veterans DeAndre Yedlin and Justen Glad. Mastroeni’s men worked as a unit to thwart multiple attacks by the Galaxy throughout the second half to secure the ever important victory. The win catapulted the squad into ninth place and earned the home side a spot in the wild card. Up next Real Salt Lake will now face the Seattle Sounders in the Wild Card match on Nov. 19th. With a win, the squad will face the top seeded Vancouver Whitecaps in a best-of-three set of matches. Kickoff for the Wild Card matchup is slated to kickoff at 8 p.m. MDT and will be streaming on Apple TV.

top.title: “I’m so tired”: Matheus Cunha dismayed by Man United’s weak mentality that cost them a win vs Aston Villa
top.description: “I’m so tired”: Matheus Cunha dismayed by Man United’s weak mentality that cost them a win vs Aston Villa Manchester United came back from two goals down in each half to eventually clinch a point after a thrilling tie against Aston Villa on Sunday. The visitors scored twice within the first five minutes of the first half and then scored another two within the opening eight minutes of the restart. On both occasions, the Red Devils managed to claw their way back, with Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans scoring in the first 45 minutes before substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu combined in added time to ensure the game finished 4-4. Will it be enough for Michael Carrick to remain at the helm? Only time will tell, but as most fans inside Old Trafford saw, the mistakes of key players let him down once again. Matheus Cunha cannot believe the weak mentality on show Diogo Dalot was at fault for two of those goals, and how the Portuguese defender has remained at the club for so long is beyond puzzling at this point. Matheus Cunha, who won the first penalty, was candid in his assessment after the game, revealing that he was tired of the way the team performed tonight. United only seemed to wake up after conceding and not from the start, and that mentality needs to change immediately, as this style of play is simply unsustainable. “I’m so tired and also disappointed. After the other night we talked about how we concede goals and have the mentality to come back in the game. Time for major changes “We did it again where we had to play like Manchester United and go forward. We showed courage but we only do this after we concede goals: showed character after conceding goals. “If we had shown that character and courage before then we will win more games. I don’t know why we are making it hard for ourselves. “We all work hard and we all want to be the best. We need to change our mentality from the beginning.” No wonder everyone wanted INEOS to strengthen the backline in the summer. Hopefully, they finally heed the call in January. top.title: Cowboys Scheme Leaves Defensive Backs Blind To Ball
top.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys secondary has gone months without a single interception by a defensive back. The unit features high-priced players and a deep roster. On Nov. 17, 2025, safety Markquese Bell secured the last interception by a Cowboys safety. That date feels like ancient history in a season that has already slipped away. The only three picks the team has this year belong to linebackers Shemar James, DeMarvion Overshown, and Dee Winters. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker told Yahoo Sports exactly why the corners and safeties are stuck in neutral. He said, “I think that just has to do with No. 1 you’re dictating coverage so you can find the ball.” Parker admitted the scheme forces defensive backs into man-to-man coverage where they cannot see the quarterback’s eyes. He added, “I mean, I think it’s as simple as that.” The team tries to use match-zone coverage, but the execution keeps them from finding the ball in the air. The Cost of Man Coverage When you force corners to play tight man coverage, you give up yards. Cornerback DaRon Bland leads the team with six pass breakups, but he has also allowed an NFL-high 438 yards. Quarterbacks have thrown for three touchdowns against him with a rating of 117.4. Parker acknowledged the issue directly. “Yeah, and we need more from him,” Parker said. He noted that Bland has been close on many contested catches but needs to finish the plays. The problem is that one mistake in the secondary puts the whole defense in the spotlight. If the linebackers are supposed to have the vision, why are the defensive backs getting burned? Parker said the linebackers play with more vision because they are in zone. Meanwhile, the corners and safeties are locked in man coverage. This leaves them blind to the quarterback’s progressions until it is too late. A Drought That Hurts the Season The Cowboys are sitting at 3-5 after losing to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime on Sunday, Nov. 1. The loss came after the team let a 24-10 lead slip away in the fourth quarter. Dak Prescott never threw a pass on the final drive after an onside kick recovery. He took a sack and watched Javonte Williams run for three yards on third-and-16. Prescott said, “Maybe the drive after the onside kick,” and called it the turning point. But the defense cannot help the offense if they cannot take the ball away. Defensive lineman Quinnen Williams called out the unit for their lack of execution. “We’re the problem. We’re the reason why we’re losing these games,” he said. Dallas opponents succeed on 51.4% of their third-down attempts. The Colts, who Dallas faces on Sunday, Nov. 8, will exploit this weakness. If the scheme does not change, the secondary will continue to give up big plays.

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are getting ready for their Week 9 matchup against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium. While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list. S Kendall Williamson, DB Deane Leonard, G Kayode Awosika, WR Theo Wease and WR Brenen Thompson are all out for the Chargers against the Texans. top.title: Jason Kelce breaks down ‘really important’ Chiefs vs Jets moment Justin Fields got wrong
top.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Justin Fields saw rare action for the Kansas City Chiefs. It did not go as planned. Former New York Jets quarterback Justin Fields has been patiently waiting for a chance. And when you are sitting behind Patrick Mahomes, that does not happen very often. The Chiefs drew up a play for Fields against his former team, bringing him in to attempt a quarterback sneak. Unfortunately he failed to execute, with the Jets stopping him short and recovering the ball for a fumble. Jason Kelce gives verdict on Justin Fields fumble A key factor for any quarterback entering the game is his chemistry with his offensive line. And this was part of where it all went wrong. Former NFL star Jason Kelce pointed to the snap from Chiefs center Creed Humphrey, noting that this started the play badly. Kelce wrote on X : “Center QB exchange is really important for QB sneak, and often overlooked. Because of the way the Center fires off the ball, the Quarterback, or whoever is taking the snap needs to get reps full speed of the snap from the center in practice to get an accurate feel.” But this does not absolve Fields from blame. Kelce noted that the backup quarterback may have got his timing all wrong. “There’s also a timing to it from the QB, not sure how many Fields has done, but he looked like he moved quickly before securing the snap there. “I like that KC is finally running it, but an unfortunate start. There’s more nuance to that play than people realize.” In the opening eight weeks of the NFL season, Justin Fields did not take a single snap. And he really needed to make this one count. A fan wrote on X: “The QB sneak/tush push with Justin Fields went so well I expect Andy Reid won’t call it again for the rest of his life.” There will be plenty for Reid and his staff to analyze on this play in the film room on Monday. Fields will just need to pray that he gets another chance. top.title: Briscoe Takes Pole As Homestead Finale Sets Stage For Title Showdown
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Chase Briscoe secured the pole position for the NASCAR Cup Series season finale, putting Joe Gibbs Racing ahead before the green flag drops on Sunday. The No. 19 Toyota driver posted a lap of 166.687 mph to edge his teammate Denny Hamlin by a razor-thin 0.017 seconds, per Motorsport.com NASCAR Cup. The result follows a year in which the team often struggled in qualifying, and Briscoe secured the win at a crucial moment. The 267-lap race at Homestead-Miami Speedway will decide the 2026 champion, and starting from the front row is the best possible spot to control the pace. A Tight Pack for the Title Three drivers remain in the championship battle, and their starting spots are closely grouped. According to Motorsport.com NASCAR Cup, Kyle Larson, who leads the points, will start fourth and requires only eight stage points to secure his third title. His closest rival, Christopher Bell, qualified sixth and trails by 67 points. Denny Hamlin is second on the front row but faces a steep climb, 70 points behind Larson with 76 points available in the race. Briscoe, who is out of title contention, stated “Yeah, our car was really good yesterday in practice too,” when discussing the speed his team found on Friday. Hamlin admitted he lost the pole by “trying to save the tires a little bit too much coming to the green,” which cost him the top spot by a fraction of a second. Brad Keselowski’s Final Bow The starting grid also marks a sad end for Brad Keselowski in his final race as a driver and co-owner for RFK Racing. Keselowski lost control of his car at the exit of Turn 4 during qualifying and spun into the inside wall, leaving him starting in the 40th and final position. “The track’s really, really slick,” said Keselowski afterward, explaining the difficult conditions that led to his crash. He added that he “Was trying to find a place that had some grip” but simply could not find it, noting, “Wish i could have that one back, but just trying to find something to be as fast as i could be.” His misfortune highlights the unforgiving nature of the 1.5-mile oval where grip is scarce. Sunday, Nov. 8, at 3 p.m. is the scheduled time for the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship race.

top.title: Bears Must Target Cornerback Riq Woolen Over Chase Young
top.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears face a critical choice before the trade deadline. While chatter swirls around a potential reunion with Khalil Mack or a move for Chase Young, the real need lies in the secondary. Due to a thumb injury sustained during the Week 8 victory, the team has just placed running back Zavier Scott on injured reserve. Scott will miss at least four games, leaving the depth chart thin. The current roster cannot afford to ignore the pass coverage holes. Why the Secondary Takes Priority Many fans want a big edge rusher to help the pass rush. However, league evaluators have shifted their view on what the team actually lacks. On Wednesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that the Bears have been linked to edge-rushers such as Khalil Mack, but a few league evaluators told him that cornerback is becoming more of a need. Adding another pass-rusher does not fix the leaks in the coverage unit. The offense has been strong, rushing for 1,206 yards through eight games. The defense must match that energy to keep Caleb Williams off the field. The Case for Woolen Over Young Reports indicate the Bears have checked in on Saints defensive end Chase Young. The NFL Rumors X account shared that the Bears and 49ers have checked in on the Saints’ Chase Young. While Young has stats to back him up, he is not the right fit for this specific roster gap. The team is also in deep competition with the Lions to acquire Riq Woolen from the Eagles. Thomas R. Petersen reported via X on Thursday that they are reportedly in deep competition with Lions to acquire Riq Woolen from the Eagles. Woolen offers a one-year solution that fits the cap and the timeline. Jacob Infante of Windy City Gridiron wrote that given the fact that Woolen is only a one-year rental, it would be surprising to see him cost more than a Day 3 draft pick. This low cost makes him a smart target compared to the high price of Young. The Window Is Closing Fast The Bears have shown they are willing to spend draft capital to win now. They already sent two first-round picks to land Jeffery Simmons. Brad Briggs added context on the injury front, noting it’s actually a thumb injury for Zavier Scott, and there is reason for hope that his stay on injured reserve will be on the shorter side. Even with that hope, the immediate void remains. The team must act to secure Woolen before the Lions steal him away. The next game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday starts the clock on this decision.

nigeria.title: Debate: ‘Agbero interests holding back Lagos public transport’ – NDC’s Doherty
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, has accused vested interests within the state’s informal transport network of frustrating efforts to modernise public transportation. Doherty made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate in Lagos on Friday organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard, where he criticised the continued reliance on ageing commercial buses and the influence of the agbero system in the state’s transport sector. He questioned why successive administrations had failed to modernise public transportation despite the thousands of rickety buses operating across Lagos. “Our public transportation system is not modernised. Thousands of rickety buses are moving around. We must ask ourselves: are these what our people deserve? Why has it taken so long to modernise public transportation?” he asked. The NDC candidate argued that the failure to reform the system was not accidental, alleging that powerful interests benefited from the existing arrangement. “In my opinion, the lack of modern transportation is not by accident. There are vested interests in operating the bus system the way it is. Many of us understand the agbero system; there is an ecosystem around it, and there is no political will to deal with that problem,” he said. Doherty, who promised to overhaul the state’s public transportation system if elected, said his administration would not be beholden to informal transport networks. “We would modernise public transportation because we would be elected by the people and not by the agbero network,” he added. nigeria.title: 2027: Nigeria needs reset, not reforms — Makinde
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said Nigeria needs a fundamental reset rather than mere reforms to address its economic, security and governance challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections. Makinde spoke on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, ahead of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Monday in the city. Explaining his position, the governor argued that reforms were insufficient where the problems in a system outweighed its strengths. “When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action. “If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point. Reform will not work in the present environment,” he said. The governor said he did not initially intend to become a politician but was motivated by concerns about the country’s future. “I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said. On the economy, Makinde identified it as the foremost priority of his proposed Reset Agenda, arguing that economic performance should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians. “The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs,” he said. He added that economic progress should be assessed by its impact on households rather than statistical indicators alone. “If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. The real test of economic performance is the condition of the people,” he said. The APM candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, education and production, while creating an enabling environment for businesses to grow and generate employment. “We must encourage our people to acquire skills and become entrepreneurs. We must invest in education and move towards intensive production. Government must provide an environment where businesses can thrive and young people can find meaningful employment,” he said. nigeria.title: Customs processes 99,839 cargo declarations in two months
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) processed 9,195 Pre-Arrival Assessment Reports (PAARs) and 99,839 Single Goods Declarations (SGDs) between September and October 2026, generating a combined revenue of approximately ₦1.42 trillion. The figures were disclosed during a joint security press briefing at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser, in Abuja. Speaking at the briefing, the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Aliyu Maiwada, said the performance reflected the Service’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, improving cargo clearance and strengthening revenue generation through digital interventions and collaboration with stakeholders. A breakdown of the figures showed that the Service processed 2,102 PAARs in September and 7,093 in October, bringing the total to 9,195. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. The Service collected ₦697.8 billion in revenue in September and ₦722.9 billion in October, amounting to ₦1.4207 trillion during the two-month period. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. At the Lilypond Export Command, export activities in the third quarter of 2026 generated a total export value of $752.85 million, compared with $586.15 million recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The statement put the increase at approximately 28.44 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of the export sector and the impact of measures aimed at facilitating non-oil exports. On enforcement, the NCS said it seized prohibited and restricted items with a combined Duty Paid Value exceeding ₦8.1 billion during the period under review. The interceptions covered various categories, including illicit drugs, pharmaceutical products, prohibited goods and petroleum products. The Service said it continued to collaborate with relevant regulatory and security agencies to ensure the appropriate handling and disposition of seized items. On its anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) responsibilities, the NCS highlighted the ongoing World Customs Organisation (WCO) Mentoring Mission, inaugurated on October 19, 2026. The four-week engagement, scheduled to run from October 18 to November 13, 2026, is designed to strengthen the capacity of the Service to identify, investigate and tackle trade-based money laundering and other illicit financial activities associated with cross-border trade. As part of the exercise, the NCS engaged six relevant agencies between October 27 and 29, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) and the National Counter Terrorism Centre. nigeria.title: Governorship Debate: Private sector cannot solve Lagos housing crisis alone – NDC’s Doherty
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, has said the private sector cannot independently address the state’s housing crisis, urging the government to take a leading role in providing affordable accommodation. Doherty made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate held in Lagos on Sunday and organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard. Doherty outlined his proposals for tackling arbitrary rent increases and improving access to affordable housing. He described arbitrary rent increases in Lagos as a form of racketeering and promised to establish an ombudsman office to address complaints and protect tenants if elected. “There is a form of racketeering. We would set up an ombudsman office to deal with this,” he said. The NDC candidate identified inadequate housing supply as one of the major factors driving rising rents in the state, arguing that housing development had failed to keep pace with growing demand. “The larger solution of the problem is due to supply. Housing supply has not kept up with growing demand,” he said. Doherty maintained that social housing should be a major government responsibility, noting that private developers alone could not meet the accommodation needs of Lagos residents. “Social housing, that is an area, where government has to be the primary driver, private housing will not do it alone,” he added. He also criticised the state government for allegedly failing to make sufficient investments in areas requiring public intervention, arguing that it had allowed the private sector to take the lead in areas where government should play a more prominent role. “One of the areas we have a problem with this government is that they don’t step up in a big way in things they should, instead allow the private sector take the lead,” he said. He said Lagos spends close to 19 billion to 20 billion on servicing its external and domestic debts, describing the burden as heavy. “The debt burden (in Lagos) is heavy. nigeria.title: Debate: ‘Lagos must learn from Japan, Venice to tackle flooding’ – GRV
nigeria.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has criticised the state government over its approach to infrastructure development, traffic management and urban planning, saying the city needs visionary leadership to address its challenges. Rhodes-Vivour, popularly known as GRV, made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate held in Lagos on Sunday and organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard. GRV outlined his proposals for improving infrastructure and preparing the state for climate-related challenges. He argued that Lagos should learn from other coastal cities, including Japan and Venice, in developing infrastructure that accommodates water flow and reduces the impact of flooding. “We lack visionary govt. They should be looking at what Japan is doing, Vernice is doing, they are coastal cities too. Vernice is standing on trees, but allows for water to flow,” he said. The ADC candidate also questioned the quality of road construction in Lagos, arguing that infrastructure projects should meet proper technical standards and include long-term maintenance plans. “What are the standards of road we are building in this city? Roads are not built to standard. We need to set proper standards and technicalities, and tie in maintenance to the construction of those road,” he said. Rhodes-Vivour further called for climate scenario planning and better communication between the government and residents to prepare Lagos for future environmental challenges. On traffic congestion, he said residents should not have to spend excessive time commuting to work, calling for an integrated transportation system that connects different parts of the state. “Traffic is not a lifestyle, we must not have to work to get to work. We need to connect the entirety of Lagos. It is a bankable project that will pay itself over the years,” he said. He proposed expanding water transportation through functional ferry terminals and increasing the availability of ferry services across the state. “We need to normalise water transportation, have ferry terminals that are not just audio, have enough water transportation. We need to normalise bicycle lanes,” he added. The ADC candidate said improved water transportation and dedicated bicycle lanes would provide residents with more commuting options and help ease pressure on Lagos roads. nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Sokoto State has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, disclosing that it is negotiating a political alliance with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) through the Nyesom Wike-led Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The PDP governorship candidate in the state, Abubakar Abdullahi Sokoto, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ meeting held at the party’s secretariat along Bodinga Road, Sokoto metropolis. Abdullahi said the proposed arrangement was aimed at mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election, declaring that the PDP in Sokoto had no alternative presidential candidate apart from the incumbent president. “Our position is to work towards President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s second-term ambition through the Rainbow Coalition, which we consider a strategic political platform for cooperation between interested PDP stakeholders and the ruling APC,” he said. He, however, maintained that the alliance would not require the PDP to abandon its political structure or candidates contesting elective positions in the state. According to him, the party would continue to mobilise support and campaign for its candidates in the 2027 elections. “We are not abandoning our party structure or our candidates. We will continue to mobilise, canvass and campaign aggressively for PDP candidates seeking elective positions across Sokoto State in 2027,” he said. Abdullahi explained that in areas where PDP candidates might lack sufficient electoral support, party members and supporters could be encouraged to support APC candidates in line with the coalition arrangement. “Where our candidates may not have the necessary electoral strength or sufficient support, our members and supporters could be encouraged to support APC candidates as part of the political understanding under the Rainbow Coalition,” he stated. He said the arrangement was intended to strengthen political cooperation and improve the electoral prospects of parties and individuals involved in the coalition. Abdullahi added that the Rainbow Coalition remained open to political groups, organisations and individuals willing to identify with its objectives, irrespective of their party affiliations. “The Rainbow Coalition is open to everybody, political groups, organisations and individuals who share our vision and are prepared to identify with its objectives, irrespective of their political backgrounds,” he said. nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funsho Doherty, has promised to make education completely free in Lagos State if elected in 2027. Doherty made the promise during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. He said his administration would focus on improving the lives of residents by equipping them with education and relevant skills. “So, our policies are aimed at capacitating the people, giving them skills, ensuring that there is no child born in Lagos who does not get an education because their parents cannot afford it. nigeria.title: ANC suffers worst-ever election result in South Africa
nigeria.description: The African National Congress (ANC), which has dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid, has recorded its worst-ever electoral performance, securing 30.76 per cent of the votes in municipal elections, according to the country’s electoral commission. The final results, announced on Sunday, showed that the party’s support had declined further, setting the stage for difficult multiparty coalition negotiations in several major cities where no party secured an outright majority. The liberal Democratic Alliance (DA), the ANC’s closest challenger and main partner in the national unity government, secured about a quarter of the votes, according to the final tally. Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of South Africa, Mosotho Moepya, said voter turnout stood at 52 per cent, six percentage points higher than the 2021 municipal elections, which were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Moepya also disclosed that voting would be repeated in one municipality after party supporters stormed a polling station and destroyed ballot papers. The outcome represents a significant decline for the party of late liberation icon Nelson Mandela, which won nearly two-thirds of the votes in South Africa’s first democratic elections in 1994. Although the ANC remains the country’s largest political party, its support has steadily declined amid widespread unemployment, which has exceeded 34 per cent, as well as crime and corruption scandals. Water shortages, electricity outages and poor service delivery were among the major issues that shaped Wednesday’s elections as voters assessed the performance of parties governing their communities. Describing the outcome as “catastrophic”, ANC Secretary-General, Fikile Mbalula, acknowledged the party’s shortcomings on Saturday. “Where we have fallen short, this movement does not dispute it. Communities have gone without water. Refuse has not been collected. Roads have not been maintained,” he said. “We have been weighed in the balance, and where we have been found wanting we dare not quarrel with the scale,” Mbalula told reporters. More than half of South Africa’s 213 municipal councils failed to produce an outright majority for any party, making coalition arrangements necessary for the formation of local governments. Previous coalitions in the country have often been characterised by internal disagreements and shifting political alliances, resulting in administrative instability and disruptions to basic services. President Cyril Ramaphosa urged political parties to prioritise the interests of communities in their coalition negotiations, warning against allowing political disagreements to disrupt essential services. “The people have spoken. Their verdict must be respected. Their concerns must be heard and their expectations must now be met,” he said on Sunday. nigeria.title: Man United stage late comeback to snatch 4-4 draw against Aston Villa
nigeria.description: Manchester United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday and potentially save manager Michael Carrick’s job. Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point, but United will spend a two-week international break in the relegation zone. Carrick’s men conceded twice inside the opening four minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson punished errors from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Red Devils rallied to level at half-time thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and Youri Tielemans’s first goal since moving to Old Trafford from Villa. A thrilling fightback from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday gave Carrick a lifeline. This time the comeback fell short as more woeful defending handed Villa two more goals inside the first eight minutes of the second period. John McGinn converted from the spot after Diogo Dalot upended Alysson before Leon Goretzka bundled in from close range. Yet, there was a final twist in the tale as Zirkzee steered home before Dorgu pounced when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki failed to connect with a corner in the 96th minute. – ‘We want new owners’ – Carrick was handed a stay of execution after a 3-0 home drubbing by Bournemouth a fortnight ago. However, he faces an anxious wait to see if the United board install a replacement before a daunting trip to Liverpool on November 22. From another tame Alysson effort less than three minutes later, Lammens could only parry and present Nicolas Jackson with a gift for his sixth goal in his last six league games. nigeria.title: Train Collision In Egypt’s Giza Kills Four, Injures 88
nigeria.description: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities. Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan. The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area. State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”. Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said. Several carriages lay on their side, AFP journalists at the scene reported. One end of a train had crumpled into a mangle of steel, while the end of the other — spliced open in the impact — had toppled off the tracks into an adjacent farm. First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed. Egyptian rescuers carry the body of a person killed in a train collision in al-Ayyat in Giza governate southern Cairo on November 8, 2026. Photo by – / AFP Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster. In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens. Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents. Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. sports.title: Michael Carrick has painfully awkward exchange with interviewer over Man United future
sports.description: Michael Carrick endured an awkward end to a post-match interview as he had an excruciating exchange about his future as Manchester United manager. Carrick had just watched his United side fight back from 4-2 down in injury time to snatch the unlikeliest of 4-4 draws with Aston Villa , having earlier come back from being 2-0 behind inside five minutes. It was a real mixed display from the Red Devils, who showed plenty of heart and character but had put themselves in bad positions due to consistently disastrous defending. The result – combined with their incredible comeback victory against Roma in midweek – has probably saved Carrick’s job, although his United side still head into this international break in the Premier League ’s bottom three, lying 18th in the table. His long-term future appears to very much still be up in the air and his post-match interview on Sky Sports with reporter Patrick Davison was an awkward watch. Carrick firstly bristled slightly when asked if United are looking at a relegation fight, saying: “No, we’re in November. I don’t like this situation we’re in, I don’t like the results we’ve had but we can definitely do something about it.” "That's not going to happen" 🗣️ Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 8, 2026 From there, things got worse, as Davison asked a lengthy question suggesting there were clearly going to be conversations about his future during the international break over the next couple of weeks, to which Carrick simply responded: "Is there?" When it was suggested that one would assume so, Carrick tersely said: “Would you?” and when he was pushed for what he thought about his situation, the Man United boss said to Davison: “You’re telling me, what do you think”. After that, the interviewer specified that he wanted to know what Carrick expected to happen in the next couple of weeks and he then gave a longer answer admitting that it wasn’t a good situation, the team haven’t won enough games but that he expects to move forward and keep working on the things they’ve been working on until this point. Michael Carrick (Reuters) Back in the Sky Sports studio, pundit Roy Keane was asked for his thoughts on the interview as a whole and the former Man United captain compared the current boss to a politician. He said: “It’s obviously difficult for the manager, he’s under pressure no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn’t say much – maybe that’s a tactic. He’s like a politician. “He’s clearly under pressure and says he knows there are things to work on but he better get moving on that... This is their worst start in however many years.”

sports.title: Caleb Williams MVP Case Hinges On Sunday Night Against Tampa Bay
sports.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images A Bears victory on Sunday could push Caleb Williams into the MVP conversation. That number trails Josh Allen, Brock Purdy, and Joe Burrow, but the gap is closing fast. Since Williams came back from a hamstring injury that sidelined him during Weeks 3 through 5, the Bears have claimed three consecutive victories. Chicago has not trailed in any of those three contests and has scored more than 30 points each time. Williams has fixed the biggest issue from his rookie year. His completion percentage has jumped from 58.1 percent in 2025 to 70.9 percent this season. Yahoo Sports noted that only Joe Burrow holds a higher rate in the entire league. At Halas Hall on Wednesday, Coach Ben Johnson informed reporters that the passing operation feels much smoother. “I think our passing game in general has been a little bit cleaner,” Johnson said. Enhanced timing and confidence linking the quarterback with his leading trio of receivers fuel this progress. The Chemistry Is Real The connection between Williams and his targets has deepened beyond the field. The group spends significant time together to build that bond. Williams explained that the communication grew because they share meals and hang out. “We hang out together. We do things together. We eat together, break bread together,” Williams said. Luther Burden III showed this grit against Seattle by catching a 1-yard touchdown to end an 8-minute, 32-second opening drive. Before the catch, Burden told Williams he did not fear the defending Super Bowl champions. “I went up to him and told him I don’t care who they is,” the wide receiver said. Williams stood up from the bench and yelled back, “I don’t give a f— who they are!” Blocking Wins Games Too The offense also relies on the receivers to do the dirty work. Rome Odunze is the key player in this new dynamic. He cleared a path for a 39-yard screen pass against Seattle that sealed the win. Kalif Raymond ran through the tunnel because Odunze made the block. “If [Odunze] doesn’t get that block, the screen doesn’t go,” Raymond said. With 14 receptions totaling 234 yards in each half, Odunze is heading toward his finest campaign in three years. sports.title: Braden Mann unleashes an 85-yard punt for Eagles
sports.description: Sunday’s game against the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles has been something of a defensive struggle. So when Nick Sirianni sent Braden Mann and the rest of the Philadelphia punt team into the game with under 30 seconds left in the first half, leading 8-6 but deep in their own territory, Sirianni probably just wanted to try and get his defense into better field position. He likely did not expect Mann to pin the Giants inside New York’s own 10-yard line. But that is exactly what happened, as Mann unleashed a booming 85-yard punt that rolled out of bounds at the Giants’ 6-yard line: BRADEN MANN WHAT A PUNT NYGvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0knmQEiDKM — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The massive punt sent FOX Sports announced Joe Davis into a state of delirium, as he declared that the kick had to be “close to the longest punt in NFL history.’ Interestingly enough, however, it does not even crack the top ten! According to Pro Football Reference, the longest punt in NFL history remains this booming 98-yard punt from Steve O’Neal of the New York Jets, back in 1969. A 92-yard punt from Shawn McCarthy of the New England Patriots comes in second, while the legendary kick from Randall Cunningham of the 1989 Eagles, which covered 91 yards, comes in third. Sammy Baugh’s 1940 punt of 85 yards comes in at No. 12 on the list, which is the mark Mann tied with this kick. You can see that full list here .

sports.title: Jorge Martin will be "almost 100% fit" in Portugal as heroic Qatar display keeps title hopes alive
sports.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin , who finished seventh in Sunday's MotoGP race at Lusail, showcased his trademark resilience throughout the weekend in Qatar. Resilience that saw him go from considering skipping the race entirely early in the week to not only competing but delaying Marc Marquez's title celebrations. Once again, MotoGP's Asian flyaway races have proven decisive in the outcome of the world championship, which is now firmly within Marquez's grasp. The Ducati rider could be crowned champion in two weeks' time, but that he failed to seal the title in Qatar was thanks to Marco Bezzecchi's speed and Martin's resilience. Read Also: MotoGP Qatar GP: Marco Bezzecchi wins as Marc Marquez has title triumph delayed Over the course of this week, Martin went from contemplating staying in Spain and missing the race at Lusail, because of the pain caused by the fracture in his right wrist, to finishing third in Saturday's sprint and seventh in Sunday's grand prix. Despite losing further ground to Marquez, the Aprilia rider demonstrated a remarkable ability to endure pain, earning praise from most of his rivals. His achievement was all the more impressive considering he started from 11th on the grid - 10th on Sunday after Francesco Bagnaia 's withdrawal - which made his task even more difficult and increased the level of risk he had to take. "I'm proud of what I've done because on Monday and Tuesday I didn't even want to come here, and in the end I managed to finish both races," said Martin in his Spanish interview on Sunday evening. "We're going to Portugal still in with a chance. It's getting harder and harder, but we're still there." Although the injury is less serious than initially feared, the limitations it imposes on him when changing direction and braking are evident, particularly over a long run or race. Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team "I can't ride properly, I can't brake properly and I can't push the bike to the limit. It was really tough towards the end. For the last three laps, I just wanted the race to be over." In the sprint, Martin benefited from his last-minute decision to use the soft rear tyre, which allowed him to gain several positions through the opening corners. On Sunday, with everyone running the same tyre specification, the playing field was more level. "There was a lot of risk in the opening corners. The key was qualifying, because starting so far back didn't help me," explained the #89, who was physically exhausted by the end of the race. "My hand is swollen up like a melon, but I think I'll be almost 100% fit in Portugal. I'm tough and stubborn. There's something inside me that keeps pushing me to fight," concluded Martin, who will head to the Algarve circuit 60 points behind Marquez and 14 ahead of Bezzecchi.
